claims.text: The WTaTiVZr alloy is equimolar, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each constituent element.
The initial WTaTiVZr HEA has a homogeneous single-phase microstructure.
The initial HEA lacks pre-existing twin boundaries and significant secondary-phase precipitates.
High-temperature nanoindentation creep and constant-load-hold testing have been applied to TaTiVWZr and compared with pure tungsten.
Mechanical loading at approximately 800–1200°C is representative of sustained plasma-facing-component service.
High-temperature loading dynamically nucleates nanoscale deformation twins in WTaTiVZr.
A high density of deformation twins refines the effective microstructure.
Intersecting twin boundaries can provide pathways for dislocation motion and cross-slip between boundaries.
Nanoscale deformation twins deflect or arrest propagating cracks.
Twin-induced microstructural refinement hinders dislocation motion and generates strain hardening.
Twin-mediated deformation produces enhanced ductility and toughness.
Nanoscale twinning is the primary cause of superior plastic strain and toughness in WTaTiVZr relative to pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten lacks significant twin-mediated deformation under the proposed high-temperature loading.
Deformed WTaTiVZr will have a higher deformation-twin density than identically loaded pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain than pure tungsten under identical high-temperature loading.
WTaTiVZr will have a lower yield stress than pure tungsten under the proposed loading.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater strain hardening and resistance to crack initiation and propagation than pure tungsten.
Thermally activated twin nucleation is feasible in WTaTiVZr at roughly 800–1200°C.
Twinning activity in WTaTiVZr may be suppressed below the stated temperature range.
Analogous alloys, including a CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy and TWIP steels, exhibit deformation-twin architectures associated with dislocation behavior, strain hardening, ductility, or toughness.
